scenarios.name: Incompatible existing buckets and disabled managed RLS fail transactionally without rewriting configuration
Exact reserve/prepare RPC exists (real missing-feature RED)
Reserve and prepare preserve publication state; exact prepared replay is unchanged
Closed arguments, sealed byte and MIME binding, running-only fence
Candidate least privilege, no client policies, immutable constraints
Restrictive Storage policies defeat broad client policies without blocking other buckets or service
Reserve and prepare transaction rollback and injected mutation failure leave no partial state
Real simultaneous reserve duplicate-id/attempt races and exact prepare replay serialize
Database clock recheck after job/candidate locks and stale prepared replay rejects expired fence
Distinct jobs sharing an uncommitted candidate ID recheck expiry after the unique-index wait
Revoked membership, tombstones, cancel and deletion reject both candidate actions
Prepare checks all supplied metadata and persisted identity; lease reuses pinned-input drift guards
Native process kill before commit rolls back; suppressed committed receipts preserve reserved/prepared evidence
Actual parent deletion preserves immutable candidate evidence and cannot prepare orphan
Global publication and local-cleanup boundary remains closed
Native HTTP streamed upload/readback, real PG candidate RPC and FFmpeg survive renewed initial lease

limits: Real isolated PG17.4 and native Unix socket; synthetic Storage tables, not real Supabase Storage/PostgREST or full migration chain.

Actual compiled TypeScript and Supabase JS call a native loopback HTTP server. A strict PostgREST-shaped adapter translates requests to parameterized real PostgreSQL as service_role; it is not actual PostgREST.

Synthetic Storage HTTP uses native streamed POST/GET and disk-backed bytes plus fixture metadata. Its HTTPS origin is rewritten only to 127.0.0.1 HTTP; real TLS, cloud Storage behavior and managed schema ownership are unqualified.

Faults suppress committed server responses or alter native HTTP response bodies; PostgreSQL wire COMMIT acknowledgement loss is not simulated. SIGKILL bypasses graceful application cleanup; only the owning harness removes its isolated temporary artifacts.

Only synthetic two-second sine-wave WebM/Opus and external native FFmpeg are qualified here; not device/long audio, deployment, backups, atomic publication or large manifests. No candidate is published or deleted and no local draft deletion is authorized.
responseLossBoundary: Actual PG commit and SIGKILL; child suppresses candidate receipt from its caller after commit. Not a dropped PostgreSQL wire COMMIT acknowledgement.
